ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the upper half of the figure is (A) a photograph of a rectangular-prism-style house; the lower half is (B) the outline of the house on grid coordinates. In figure (B), it can be read that the two points of the left vertical edge are (0,3) and (0,0), the endpoints of the long edge near the farther right vertical edge are (22,10) and (22,-3), and the right end face also has (26,3) and (26,0). The roof edge in the long direction corresponds in the figure to the line segment from (0,3) to (22,10), and the ground edge in the long direction corresponds to the line segment from (0,0) to (22,-3). Then reason: the two actual horizontal edges in the long direction, after being extended in the perspective drawing, intersect at the same vanishing point, and the horizontal line on which this vanishing point lies is the horizon line. The equation of the roof edge is y = 3 + (7/22)x; the equation of the ground edge is y = -(3/22)x. Set the two equations equal: 3 + (7/22)x = -(3/22)x, obtaining x = -6.6, and substituting back gives y = 0.9. Therefore the height of the horizon line in the image coordinates is y = 0.9. On the left vertical edge, y=0 corresponds to an actual 0 meters above the ground, and y=3 corresponds to the actual house height H=3 meters. The proportion of the horizon line in vertical height is (0.9-0)/(3-0), so the camera height above the ground is 3 × 0.9/3 = 0.9 meters.

raw_record.question_text: These days, there are so many stylish rectangular home-designs (see figure A). It is possible from the outline of those houses in their picture to estimate with good precision where the camera was. Consider an outline in one photograph of a rectangular house which has height $H=3$ meters (see figure B for square-grid coordinates). Assume that the camera size is negligible, how high above the ground (in meters) was the camera at the moment this picture was taken?

method.method_draft: Use the vanishing point of one horizontal direction to locate the horizon, then convert its position on a vertical edge into real height. From figure B, read the long side roof/floor edges as the lines through (0,3)-(22,10) and (0,0)-(22,-3). Their equations are y=3+(7/22)x and y=-(3/22)x, so their extensions meet at y=0.9. This y-coordinate is the horizon height in the picture. On the left vertical edge, the ground and roof are marked at y=0 and y=3, corresponding from the text to physical heights 0 m and H=3 m. Since the horizon cuts a vertical edge at the same fraction as the camera height, the camera height is 3*(0.9-0)/(3-0)=0.9 m.
